children: Roblox reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.57 billion, up 15.6% year over year, while net loss attributable to common stockholders narrowed to $227 million from $256 million. Diluted loss per share improved to $0.32 from $0.37.
¹ Reported as “Revenue”. ² Reported as “Net loss attributable to common stockholders”. ³ Reported as “loss per share attributable to common stockholders, basic and diluted”.
Revenue growth was primarily driven by amortization of prior-period bookings. Bookings declined to $1.70 billion, while average daily unique payers fell to 1.8 million from 2.3 million.
Roblox continued developing age checks for chat and launched Roblox Kids and Roblox Select, age-based accounts with tailored games and safeguards.
The company raised creator payouts and increased the Developer Exchange rate for eligible spending by age-checked U.S. adults.
Roblox plans continued investment in infrastructure, AI-enabled safety and moderation, and tools to help creators build and reach users.
